issues.legal_issue: An ex parte decree granting specific performance after the defendants failed to file a written statement remains executable when it grants the specific relief sought and contains no jurisdictional defect, notwithstanding a challenge that its terms are vague or contingent.
material_facts: The vendors accepted earnest money and delivered possession of a garage under an agreement to sell the property.

The vendors did not file a written statement despite opportunities, and the court, after referring to the plaint, pronounced judgment under Order VIII Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and granted the specific-performance relief sought against them.
The decree had attained finality after an appeal was dismissed as time-barred and an application to set aside the ex parte decree was dismissed.
The vendors challenged execution on the grounds that the decree lacked a formal adjudication and was vague or contingent; no jurisdictional defect or nullity was established.
issues.conclusion: The decree is valid and executable against the vendors, but only to the extent of their shares; the alternative damages relief does not apply because specific performance was granted. The claim to a share by the person against whom no relief was decreed depends on the outcome of his pending suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(2) and Order VIII Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a decree pronounced after failure to file a written statement is not deprived of the force of a decree merely because it is ex parte. A decree must be construed to give effect to its true import; where it is ambiguous, the executing court may consult the judgment and, if necessary, the pleadings, but may not go behind or beyond the decree. Topanmal Chhotamal v. Kundomal Gangaram supports this approach.

rule.if: execution_of_specific_performance_decree and defendants_failed_to_file_written_statement and court_considered_claim_and_granted_specific_performance and not established_jurisdictional_defect

predicates.execution_of_specific_performance_decree: A party sought execution of a decree granting specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.defendants_failed_to_file_written_statem: The defendants did not file a written statement despite being given an opportunity to do so.
predicates.court_considered_claim_and_granted_speci: The court considered the claim presented and granted the specific-performance relief sought.
predicates.established_jurisdictional_defect: A jurisdictional defect rendering the decree a nullity was established.

issues.definition: When a party seeks execution of a specific-performance decree, the defendants failed to plead despite an opportunity, the court considered and granted the claim, and no jurisdictional defect is established, the decree is executable against those bound by it.

issues.legal_issue: On an application to rescind a specific-performance contract, the court must balance the parties’ conduct and the equitable consequences of delay and appreciation in property value, and may adjust the terms of performance or provide for compensation and discharge.
material_facts: The decree did not fix a time for payment of the balance, which was payable in connection with execution and registration of the conveyance after the vendors obtained the required permission and addressed the associated charge.

The vendors did not complete their obligations, including paying the required charge, and the purchaser also failed to take prompt steps to obtain directions or tender the balance; the purchaser first made an oral request to deposit it many years after the decree.
The purchaser deposited the balance and an amount toward the charge only after obtaining permission during the appeals, without the vendors having an opportunity to respond to that oral request.
The property value and the charge payable by the vendors had increased substantially, and the vendors sought rescission on the ground that the purchaser had not deposited the balance.
The delay and defaults were attributable to both sides, and the trial court had not addressed the substantial increased liability when dismissing the rescission application.
issues.conclusion: The rescission application required an equitable order rather than its dismissal without balancing the consequences. The purchaser was directed to pay the vendors an amount based on the prevailing notified land value and to meet the increased charge. If the purchaser did not make the required deposit, the vendors could instead deposit compensation calculated on that basis, after which they would be discharged from their contractual and decree obligations; if the purchaser deposited the amount, execution was to be completed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 empowers the court that passed a specific-performance decree to rescind the contract as justice requires and reflects the court’s continuing control over the decree. The court must balance equity and the parties’ defaults; where no time for performance is specified, Section 46 of the Contract Act, 1872 requires performance within a reasonable time. Hungerford Investment Trust Ltd. v. Haridas Mundhra recognizes continuing control over the decree; Nirmala Anand v. Advent Corporation (P) Ltd. permits reasonable equitable conditions, including an additional payment; and Satya Jain v. Anis Ahmed Rushdie holds that delay and appreciation alone do not justify denying specific performance, though they may support additional compensation, with fairness and the parties’ conduct guiding the result.

rule.if: application_to_rescind_after_specific_performance_decree and substantial_delay_and_property_appreciation and purchaser_delayed_tender_or_directions and vendors_failed_to_complete_obligations and increased_property_charge_created_unfair_burden

predicates.application_to_rescind_after_specific_pe: A party applied to the court that made a specific-performance decree to rescind the contract.
predicates.substantial_delay_and_property_appreciat: A substantial period passed before completion while the value of the property increased significantly.
predicates.purchaser_delayed_tender_or_directions: The purchaser did not promptly tender the balance or seek directions needed to complete performance.
predicates.vendors_failed_to_complete_obligations: The vendors failed to carry out obligations required of them to complete the conveyance.
predicates.increased_property_charge_created_unfair: A substantial increase in a charge required for completion created an inequitable burden on the vendors.

issues.definition: Where a rescission application follows substantial delay and appreciation, the purchaser delayed taking completion steps, the vendors also failed to perform, and increased charges created an unfair burden, performance may be conditioned on an equitable value adjustment or replaced by compensatory discharge.

issues.legal_issue: Execution of a decree cannot proceed against a person who was named in the suit but against whom the operative decree granted no relief.
material_facts: A minor was impleaded as a defendant in the specific-performance suit, but the decree expressly granted relief against the other defendants only and stated that no relief was sought against him.
Execution was sought against the minor, who claimed an interest in the property and had a separate suit concerning that claim pending.
The High Court held that execution could not be pursued against him because there was no decree against him, and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal challenging that result.
issues.conclusion: Execution cannot proceed against the person who was not made subject to the decree; his claim to an interest in the property depends on the outcome of his pending suit.
issues.legal_principle: Execution must remain within the terms of the decree and cannot impose liability on a person against whom the decree grants no relief. The rule that a court cannot go behind or beyond the decree, applied in construing decrees as discussed in Topanmal Chhotamal v. Kundomal Gangaram, supports this result.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party sought to enforce a court decree against a person.
predicates.person_named_as_defendant: The person was named as a defendant in the proceeding that resulted in the decree.
predicates.operative_decree_grants_no_relief_agains: The operative decree granted no relief against that person.

issues.definition: If execution is sought against a person who was named as a defendant but was not made subject to the operative decree, execution cannot proceed against that person.
